title: Remote Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Entanglement Generation between Trapped Ions
authors: Haruki Aoki, Kazufumi Tanji, Shohei Kiryu, Masahiro Takeoka, Junko Ishi-Hayase
abstract: Distributing entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits is an important capability for scalable quantum networks. We propose a heralded protocol for generating remote entanglement between Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill qubits encoded in the motional modes of spatially separated trapped ions, using the internal electronic states to interface the motional qubits with emitted photons. We derive the protocol for single-rail and polarization photonic encodings and evaluate the effects of finite GKP squeezing, photon loss, photon recoil, motional heating, and motional dephasing on the decoded logical state. Moreover, we numerically analysed the fidelity of distributed logical Bell-pair fidelity. We find that one can achieve more than 95% of fidelity in the realistic situation. The protocol combines motional-control and photonic-networking operations that have already been demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments.
summary: This paper presents a heralded protocol to generate remote entanglement between GKP logical qubits encoded in trapped-ion motional modes. It details a three-step process utilizing internal electronic states to mediate entanglement transfer via emitted photons. The analysis rigorously quantifies the achievable logical fidelity, demonstrating performance above 95% even when incorporating realistic noise sources like heating and photon loss.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a scalable method to distribute entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits, which is crucial for building quantum networks.
main_result: The authors propose a heralded protocol achieving a logical Bell-state fidelity exceeding 95% in realistic trapped-ion settings, even when accounting for various noise sources.
method: The protocol uses a three-step process involving local entanglement generation, conversion to a motion-ion-photon GHZ state, and final remote entanglement projection via photon interference.
model_or_system: The system is trapped ions, where Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits are encoded in the motional modes. The process interfaces these motional qubits with emitted photons using the internal electronic states.
key_observables: Logical Bell-state fidelity ($F_L$), which is evaluated using Stabilizer Subsystem Decomposition (SSSD).
important_parameters: Noise parameters include photon recoil, motional heating rate ($\dot{ ar{n}}$), and motional dephasing rate ($\kappa_{\phi}$).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the combination of motional-control and photonic-networking operations are already demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments, and the BSM detectors lack temporal resolution.

paper_structure: The paper details the three-step protocol (local entanglement, GHZ generation, remote projection), derives the necessary Hamiltonians and noise channels (recoil, heating, dephasing), and concludes with a numerical analysis of the logical fidelity under realistic noise conditions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical implementation challenges of quantum networking by providing a concrete, high-fidelity protocol for distributing entanglement using established trapped-ion platforms.
